name: Security, Trust, Diagnostics, and Recovery
purpose: Define Beta 1.0 authentication, encryption-key separation, local-instance trust, backup/recovery verification, prohibited-secret boundaries, and non-authoritative sanitized diagnostics without taking ownership from persistence or domain services.

decisions.decision: Local Administrator authentication credentials, live-data encryption key material, portable-backup recovery material, per-run authentication identity, and any future device credential-provider reference are separate authorities with separate lifecycles.
The Local User Profile authenticates the one local administrator but never becomes the cryptographic authority for live operational data or portable backups.

Live operational data is protected under an independently generated Windows-protected data-encryption key; password change must not require rewriting domain identity or treating the password as the data key.
Portable backup sets are independently encrypted and self-verifiable; restore verification and compatibility checks complete before live-data mutation begins.
Loopback binding is necessary but insufficient for runtime trust. Launcher/control operations require exact origin, process-birth identity, canonical data ownership and authenticated run identity.
Reusable device/authentication secrets are prohibited from ordinary domain, evidence, Notes, workbook, audit-payload and diagnostic data. Beta 1.0 exposes no device-credential or SSH controls.

Diagnostics are structured external observability records, never authoritative application audit/history. Diagnostic failure may lose diagnostics for otherwise valid work but cannot convert a domain, migration, authorization, audit or integrity failure into success.

Sensitive-data prevention occurs before diagnostic queuing/sinks through allowlisted structured context and semantic classification; redaction is defense in depth, and sanitizer failure never falls back to raw data.
SOMA performs no automatic diagnostic/support upload. Any future support export is explicit, previewed, re-sanitized and non-authoritative.

Security controls fail closed for authentication, authorization, instance identity, integrity, restore verification and prohibited-secret disclosure while retaining bounded diagnosable failure states.
